free_tier.stated: We provide this service for free! Also, each user of the tunnel broker is provided with his own IPv6 network of size / 48.

egress.terms: no traffic allowance is published anywhere or company pages read; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: 'The broker's website contains a large number of different configurations for various operating systems and equipment.'
tooling: iproute2 or any 6in4-capable router; the site publishes per-OS configurations
chaining: pairs with any free VM that has a public IPv4, since 6in4 needs one; it is the cheapest way to give such a VM a routed /48.
binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary is stated: the /48 is free, no byte meter is published and no rate is published. The gate is a capability rather than a quota: 'To work the tunnel, you need to have a public ("honest") IPv4 address', so a client behind CGNAT cannot use it at all. Reachability is IPv6-only.

identity_cost.detail: https://tb.netassist.ua/ offers 'register a new user (it's FREE!)'; the login page warns 'Please, do NOT use hotmail and live.com mail accounts! They've baned us for some unknown reasons'.

reliability_note: single country, single PoP; the operator states that hotmail and live.com mail domains are blocked on its side.
confidence_note: the /48, the price and the public-IPv4 requirement are documented from the vendor page; the transport protocol is only named by the handwiki broker list, not by NetAssist, and that third-party statement is what holds the record at reported. A vendor page naming 6in4 or GRE, or a provisioned tunnel, would raise it.

evidence.proved: 'We provide this service for free! Also, each user of the tunnel broker is provided with his own IPv6 network of size / 48.'
'To work the tunnel, you need to have a public ("honest") IPv4 address.'
registration is a free web account; the site warns that hotmail and live.com addresses are blocked
dynamic IPv4 endpoints are handled by an autochangeip URL with a sub-60-second update time
NetAssist listed with a /48 subnet and 6in4 as the transport
'Please, fill in this form to get your FREE IPv6 tunnel.' and the two fields a new account supplies

notes: One PoP (Kiev), operating since 2011, page footer says 2011-2026. A BGP-enabled tunnel is available by email for clients with their own AS and address space. The company sells /48 PI space plus an ASN for EUR 300/year, which is a separate product from the free broker. The site is a 2011-era broker with an email login, an IPv4 endpoint field and a dynamic-IP updater, which is the classic protocol-41 shape described in the Wikipedia tunnel broker article; that is inference, not evidence.

extras.wg_detail: no WireGuard option appears on any NetAssist page read today
extras.volume_stated: no traffic allowance is published anywhere or company pages read
extras.transit_note: NetAssist carries the traffic on AS29632 from Kiev.
